items.title: The Death Of The Button: Why The Best Interface Is No Interface
items.summary_original: Ever since the commercialisation of the Graphical User Interface pioneered by systems like the Xerox Star and popularised by the original Apple Macintosh , software has relied heavily on point-and-click interactions. If you wanted to book a trip, buy a pair of shoes, or research a health symptom, you were expected to navigate a labyrinth of user interfaces. You click menus, adjust range sliders, fill out multi-step forms, deal with cookie pop-ups, and open dozens of browser tabs just to cross-reference basic information. We have become accustomed to spending more time managing the software rather than actually achieving our goals. That contract is officially changing. items.summary_de: Seit der Kommerzialisierung der grafischen Benutzeroberfläche, die durch Systeme wie den Xerox Star vorangetrieben und durch den ursprünglichen Apple Macintosh populär gemacht wurde, ist Software stark auf Point-and-Click-Interaktionen angewiesen. Wenn Sie eine Reise buchen, ein Paar Schuhe kaufen oder ein Gesundheitssymptom recherchieren wollten, wurde von Ihnen erwartet, dass Sie sich durch ein Labyrinth von Benutzeroberflächen navigieren. Sie klicken auf Menüs, passen Bereichsregler an, füllen mehrstufige Formulare aus, kümmern sich um Cookie-Popups und öffnen Dutzende Browser-Registerkarten, nur um grundlegende Informationen zu vergleichen. Wir haben uns daran gewöhnt, mehr Zeit mit der Verwaltung der Software zu verbringen, als tatsächlich unsere Ziele zu erreichen. Dieser Vertrag ändert sich offiziell. Angetrieben durch Fortschritte in der künstlichen Intelligenz und großen Sprachmodellen ist eine neue Generation von Web-Tools auf dem Vormarsch

items.title: how interior design evolves to meet new human behaviors and shifting habits
items.summary_original: CHANGING EXPECTATIONS IN INTERIOR DESIGN Shifting daily routines, remote work, and changing social habits are reshaping how we experience interior architecture. Traditional boundaries across homes , hotels , hospitals , offices and schools are dissolving to support multifaceted lives. Whether a compact apartment floor plan shifts to accommodate working from home, or a public destination merges dining with quiet retreat, spaces are being asked to accommodate different uses, experiences, and ways of interacting. As Cheryl Durst, CEO of the International Interior Design Association and an iF DESIGN AWARD juror, notes, designers are moving away from traditional labels to focus on how people actually occupy space. items.title: rodolphe parente and marion mailaender revive the spirit of 1985 paris sports club
items.summary_original: rodolphe parente and marion mailaender reimagine ken club Rodolphe Parente and Marion Mailaender reimagine Paris’ Ken Club as an architecture in motion, bringing the 1985 identity of the fitness and social club into a contemporary setting opposite the Eiffel Tower . The architects approach the past as an architectural remix, shaping a place where the visual language and atmosphere of the 1980s are sampled, reworked, and given a new rhythm. Parente and Mailaender imagine the club almost as a film set built to last, recreating the atmosphere of another era without turning the interiors into a period replica. Saturated colors, rounded forms, reflective surfaces, and theatrical contrasts between light and shadow give the spaces a sense of movement. all images by Mathias Benguigui, unless state

items.title: The kinesiologist who now animates furniture: how Kent Wood found motion design's full circle
items.summary_original: The founder of Kwoo Studio discusses how he's made a name for himself after a career pivot and a move across the Atlantic. items.summary_original: Mix Interiors, the leading UK title for commercial interior design and architecture, published bi-monthly since 2000, has been given a full editorial redesign. The project reworks the magazine’s covers, typography and grid while keeping the signature features that have defined it for more than two decades. In the redesign, three key editorial elements are playfully responsive to content: headers, colour and composition. Headers and colour function as typographic and chromatic responses to the tone and content of each article, while composition shifts spread to spread — scale, placement and pacing each responding to the editorial character of the piece. Danna Gutiérrez is a visual artist from Cali, Colombia, now based in Bogota, working under the name Gallina Clueka – an experimental multidisciplinary project that treats drawing as a starting point rather than a destination with an end point. What begins as an image on paper regularly ends up in a different form as a ceramic vessel, a piece of jewellery, a print or a textile. "I like thinking of my drawings as something that can leave the paper, become something that can be touched and used, and eventually inhabit other people's spaces," she says. items.summary_original: Die KI-Kennzeichnungspflicht ist jetzt da – und der GWA hat dazu eine Umfrage gestartet. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Agenturen mehr Beratungsleistung schaffen müssen und dass sich auf Consumer-Seite momentan noch ein ungenaues Bild abzeichnet. Die KI-Kennzeichnungspflicht ist offiziell Realität. Doch welchen Einfluss hat die neue Regulierung auf die Werbebranche? Eine aktuelle Umfrage des Gesamtverbands Kommunikationsagenturen (GWA), die zwischen dem 31. Juli und dem 31. August 2026 unter den Mitgliedsagenturen durchgeführt wurde, liefert Antworten. Die Grundstimmung ist erstmal positiv: Rund 66 Prozent der befragten Agenturen begrüßen die neue Kennzeichnungspflicht. Zudem geben 85 Prozent an, dass die Regeln keinerlei negativen Auswirkungen auf den tatsächlichen Einsatz von KI in ihren Ka

items.title: Shelf Life 126: Have Private Label Brands Become More Desirable Than Their Counterparts?
items.summary_original: Store brands used to be the compromise you settled for, but now they're the thing people seek out. A new report from Pearlfisher calls it the "cult threshold," the moment private label stops apologizing for itself and starts building the kind of cachet that makes Kirkland Signature a status symbol and Trader Joe's tote bags a cultural moment. Here's what's driving the shift, and what it means for the designers building it. Hier erfahren Sie, was den Wandel vorantreibt und was er für die Designer bedeutet, die ihn entwickeln. items.title: purple fabric reflects sunlight and releases heat to stay cool in the sun
items.summary_original: A PURPLE TEXTILE REFLECTS SUNLIGHT AND RELEASES HEAT A new purple cooling fabric developed by researchers at Zhengzhou University in China and the University of Adelaide in Australia challenges the idea that the coolest option must be white. The experimental textile combines color with passive radiative cooling, using microscopic fibers containing a metal-organic framework and zinc oxide nanoparticles to reflect much of the sun’s energy while releasing heat. In Thomke Meyer's illustrations, you'll spot hair whipping sideways, vines coiling and unravelling across a page, figures leaning mid-stride as if the wind is about to set them afloat. items.title: Why Studio Kiln swapped Cornwall for London
items.summary_original: The award-winning studio has spent years proving creativity doesn't need a postcode. So why are they now heading for the Big Smoke? Even in 2026, some people get sniffy about the idea of running a design studio outside of London. Especially somewhere like Falmouth, 300 miles away on the west coast of England. And yet that's exactly where Studio Kiln decided to set up shop, back in 2022. And since then, it's all gone surprisingly well. The creative practice has won a number of awards and built a strong reputation for its branding and digital work, such as its particle system for BAFTA . It's all powerful proof that you don't need to be anywhere near the M25 to prosper. So our ears pricked up when we heard, recently, that the studio was taking on space in London. items.title: when the power goes out, how can the architecture keep a house cool?
items.summary_original: COOLING MOVES BACK INTO THE HOUSE At Jalmanjar Farmhouse outside Ahmedabad , cooling begins with a perforated facade of compressed earth blocks. This outer skin filters the sun while windcatchers draw air through the enclosure. Behind it, verandas and balconies occupy the shaded space between the outer jali and the inner rooms, and an open courtyard cuts through the center of the plan. The house does have active systems, but much of its thermal work has already started in the wall and in the void before a machine enters the equation. Before cooling became an appliance, it was an integrated part of the building. items.title_de: Wie kann die Architektur ein Haus kühl halten, wenn der Strom ausfällt?
items.summary_de: Die Kühlung geht zurück ins Haus. Im Jalmanjar Farmhouse außerhalb von Ahmedabad beginnt die Kühlung mit einer perforierten Fassade aus komprimierten Erdblöcken. Diese Außenhaut filtert die Sonne, während Windfänger Luft durch das Gehäuse saugen. Dahinter befinden sich Veranden und Balkone, die den schattigen Raum zwischen dem Außenjali und den Innenräumen einnehmen, und ein offener Innenhof durchschneidet die Mitte des Grundrisses. Das Haus verfügt zwar über aktive Systeme, aber ein Großteil der thermischen Arbeit hat bereits in der Wand und im Hohlraum begonnen, bevor eine Maschine ins Spiel kommt. Bevor die Kühlung zu einem Gerät wurde, war sie ein integrierter Bestandteil des Gebäudes. Öffnungen waren den vorherrschenden Winden ausgesetzt, da die Luft einen Weg durch das Haus brauchte und Höfe kühlere Bereiche in der Nähe der bewohnten Räume bildeten. Dickes Mauerwerk verlangsamte den Wärmedurchgang
